tools.name: list_services
tools.description: Every service, in full. Use this for "what does he do" and anything else that wants the whole picture; search_services is for a symptom and will say so rather than guess when a question is too broad for it.

tools.name: search_services
tools.description: Find services by what the visitor is trying to solve. Matches the symptom, the platform, or the name of a system — "stock not matching the warehouse", "NetSuite", "failed renewals".

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: Everything about one service: what it covers, what it excludes, the projects behind it, and the questions people ask.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Projects, filterable. Use this to answer "has he done X" rather than guessing from the service descriptions.

tools.name: get_facts
tools.description: Verified figures — years working, projects completed, how many were built from scratch, response times. Counts are computed rather than stored, so they cannot go stale.

tools.name: what_is_not_offered
tools.description: What is explicitly out of scope, and why. Worth checking before recommending him for something.

tools.name: how_to_get_in_touch
tools.description: The three ways in — book a call, describe a project in writing, or report something broken now — with what each is for and the response time.

tools.name: submit_urgent_request
tools.description: Report a site that is broken now — checkout failing, payments declined, a critical error, a white screen, locked out of wp-admin, an update that broke the site, a hack or a malware warning. Triaged the same day, within eight hours, weekends included, across European, US, Canadian and Australian hour

tools.name: submit_project_inquiry
tools.description: Describe a project in writing and get a reply within 24 hours, weekends included. For work that is planned rather than broken: a rebuild, a migration, an integration, a second opinion on code somebody else wrote. Use submit_urgent_request instead when a site is down or losing money now. Submits imme

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Free consultation slots over the next few weeks. Read-only — call this before proposing a time so the suggestion is real rather than invented.

tools.name: request_consultation
tools.description: Propose a booking. This does NOT book anything and does NOT reserve the time: it emails the person a confirmation link valid for thirty minutes, and only their click puts it in the calendar. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "submit_urgent_request" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Report a site that is broken now — checkout failing, payments declined, a critical error, a white screen, locked out of wp-admin, an update that broke the site,…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "submit_urgent_request" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Report a site that is broken now — checkout failing, payments declined, a critical error, a white screen, locked out of wp-admin, an update that broke the site,…

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_project_inquiry, request_consultation · Public sink: submit_urgent_request, submit_project_inquiry, request_consultation.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_project_inquiry, request_consultation · Public sink: submit_urgent_request, submit_project_inquiry, request_consultation

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
